headline: People Activism Forum questions India's NCAP spending as air pollution linked to over 2 million deaths
dek: The group said most National Clean Air Programme funds went to road-dust management and called for coordinated, mission-mode action across ministries, as was done during COVID.
body:
The People Activism Forum said in a post on X that air pollution has consequences similar to those of SARS-CoV-2 and COVID-19. It stated that air pollution accounted for more than 2 million deaths in India in 2023.

The group also commented on how money under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) has been spent. Of the Rs 13,415 crore allocated to control air pollution, it said around 68% has gone to road-dust management, 14% to transport, and 12% to waste management and biomass burning. It said this spending has produced no appreciable improvement.

The forum argued that success should not be judged by fund allocation or announced restrictions. It said the measure should be actual reductions in population exposure and improvements in health. It called for mission-mode, coordinated implementation by the environment, health, transport, power, agriculture and urban development ministries, as happened during COVID.

The post described air pollution as far more than a respiratory health concern. According to the forum, it contributes to cardiovascular disease, stroke, chronic respiratory disorders, lung cancer and diabetes. The post tagged the Commission for Air Quality Management and several Indian government ministries, as well as the Prime Minister's Office.
key_quote: Success cannot be measured by fund allocation and announced restrictions
